auditFindings.summary: The current Svelte surface mixes docs navigation, token inspection, package metadata, and target-app UI into one monolithic screen.
auditFindings.impact: GPUI would end up reproducing docs-shell noise instead of a clean shared target app.

auditFindings.summary: The main preview app entry is a 3328-line single Svelte component backed by a 2085-line global stylesheet.
auditFindings.impact: The current surface is difficult to reason about, hard to contract, and too coupled for efficient cross-runtime parity work.

auditFindings.summary: The old preview was broad but shallow, so the rebuilt shared demo must close primitive coverage gaps instead of leaving long-tail exports as contract-only surfaces.
auditFindings.impact: Without direct primitive coverage inside the shared demo shell, GPUI parity would still be forced to guess at long-tail exported controls.

auditFindings.summary: Catalog, token summary, and token inspector are useful docs utilities but should not sit inside the target app GPUI is trying to match.
auditFindings.impact: Side-by-side review gets diluted by sections that are not the main shared Loophole-facing UI target.

auditFindings.summary: The current review surface is organized as section demos rather than a coherent app with screens, flows, and stable region ownership.
auditFindings.impact: The current surface demonstrates parts, but not one believable app that both Svelte and GPUI can implement as the same UI.

auditFindings.summary: The demo still relies heavily on preview-specific shell glue, state controls, and inspection layout rather than treating the shared components as the main screen-building blocks.
auditFindings.impact: Component adoption is harder to read and parity work risks targeting scaffolding instead of the shared public surface.

targetShapeFreeze.description: A coherent contract-owned demo app that demonstrates the same UI in Svelte and GPUI without docs-shell noise.

requiredScreens.goal: Establish shell hierarchy, global controls, and identity without mixing docs navigation and token-inspector utilities.
Demonstrate fields, actions, validation, banners, and status posture through one realistic screen.
Demonstrate list, grid, table, filtering, bulk action, and empty-state posture through one coherent browse surface.
Demonstrate headers, metadata rows, cards, breadcrumbs, and related companion content as one detail workflow.
Demonstrate selection flows, media thumbnails, preview fallback, and embed posture through one media-adjacent workflow.
Demonstrate command discovery, dock or split hierarchy, panel surfaces, tabs, and shell status in one workstation screen.

requiredRules: The shared demo app must be separable from docs-shell and token-inspector utilities.
The demo must prefer real public primitives, composites, and workstation components over ad-hoc HTML or preview-specific shells.
The rebuilt Svelte demo must directly preview every public primitive export somewhere inside the shared demo shell.
Each screen must have an explicit state matrix and parity checklist instead of section-local demo glue alone.
The Svelte demo must become the clean parity target before GPUI demo implementation begins.
nonGoals: Do not turn the shared demo app into a full published docs site.
Do not treat docs-shell utilities as required demo parity targets.
Do not force every export into its own detached screen if that hurts coherence.
